validity.recommendation: The row is a capacity upgrade of the main line with no new pipe. Keep length at 0 and diameter blank.
validity.researcher_notes: This is the compressor-station upgrade of the main line for the Far Eastern gas route to China. An Interfax report says the main line capacity rises through compressor stations. The 10 bcm/y capacity matches Neftegaz.

fills.researcher_notes: Neftegaz of 19 November 2024 says the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok gas pipeline is the base of the Far Eastern route and that gas deliveries by that route are planned to start at the end of January 2027. So the upgrade is still planned. The link is a Wayback copy.

The sheet says 2025. Neftegaz of 19 November 2024 says deliveries by the Far Eastern route are planned for the end of January 2027. An earlier Neftegaz piece from 2023 expected full capacity in 2025. The newer source is used. The link is a Wayback copy.
Neftegaz says the Far Eastern route will carry 10 billion cubic meters a year of gas. Interfax in 2022 gives the same figure for the contract. The link is a Wayback copy.
Interfax in 2022 says the main line has already been widened and that its capacity will grow by building and starting compressor stations. No new pipe is described, so length stays zero.
Neftegaz of 19 November 2024 reports that the government assigned this work to Gazprom. The link is a Wayback copy.
Neftegaz of 19 November 2024 reports that the government assigned this work to Gazprom. No page gives a share. The link is a Wayback copy.
